migration_steps.activity: Establish PQC program office, governance, and executive sponsorship; define scope for VPN, email, and document signing; allocate budget and assign accountable owners.

Conduct comprehensive cryptographic discovery and inventory refresh using automated network scanning, endpoint agents, and configuration management database reconciliation; identify all RSA-4096 and ECDSA usage across VPN, email, and document signing.
prerequisites: Network access and change approval for discovery scans

migration_steps.activity: Perform cryptographic risk assessment and data classification; map inventory findings to business functions, data sensitivity, and regulatory requirements; prioritize migration candidates.

Develop PQC migration architecture and target-state design using NIST FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) for key establishment and FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) for digital signatures; define hybrid transition modes and crypto-agility requirements.

Engage Cisco and Microsoft formally to obtain PQC roadmaps, firmware/software support commitments, FIPS validation status, and delivery timelines; issue requests for information and contractual change requests.
Build PQC skills through training and hiring: NIST PQC standards, hybrid key exchange, ML-KEM/ML-DSA implementation, and crypto-agility operations; establish lab environment for testing.
Evaluate and select PQC-capable replacement or overlay solutions for Cisco routers that cannot be firmware-upgraded; assess hardware refresh, external crypto modules, or network redesign options.

Conduct non-production lab testing of ML-KEM and ML-DSA in VPN, email, and document signing workflows using available software libraries and vendor previews; validate interoperability and performance.
prerequisites: PQC libraries available (e.g., OpenSSL 3.5+ with ML-KEM/ML-DSA)
Vendor preview or test builds obtained where available

migration_steps.activity: Procure PQC-capable hardware and software based on evaluation results; execute contracts with vendors that have confirmed FIPS-validated PQC support.
prerequisites: Vendor PQC support confirmed with evidence
Budget approved and procurement vehicles in place

migration_steps.activity: Pilot PQC migration in a limited production segment (e.g., one VPN concentrator pair and a small user group) during approved change windows outside the Nov 15–Jan 15 freeze; measure performance and operational impact.
Deploy PQC for VPN key establishment using ML-KEM in hybrid mode across production Cisco infrastructure (or replacements) in phased waves during approved change windows.
prerequisites: Vendor PQC firmware/hardware validated and FIPS certified

migration_steps.activity: Deploy PQC for document signing using ML-DSA via updated signing applications and certificate authority integration; migrate signing workflows in phases.
prerequisites: ML-DSA library and CA support validated

migration_steps.activity: Deploy PQC for email signing and encryption using ML-DSA and ML-KEM once Microsoft releases and validates PQC plugin for Exchange; phased rollout across user base.
prerequisites: Microsoft PQC plugin released and FIPS validated

migration_steps.activity: Decommission legacy RSA-4096 and ECDSA cryptographic configurations; update policies, procedures, and inventory; conduct final compliance audit against executive order mandate.

blockers.blocker: Cryptographic inventory is outdated and incomplete.
blockers.reason: Without an accurate inventory, migration scope, risk prioritization, and vendor requirements cannot be reliably defined; unknown cryptographic dependencies may cause migration failures or missed systems.
blockers.resolution_required: Deploy automated cryptographic discovery tools, reconcile with CMDB, conduct manual surveys of all business units, and validate findings through network scans and endpoint agents.

blockers.blocker: Cisco routers do not support firmware upgrades for PQC.
blockers.reason: The existing hardware cannot run PQC algorithms, so VPN key establishment using ML-KEM cannot be deployed on current infrastructure without hardware replacement or overlay solutions.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain Cisco official statement on PQC roadmap and hardware compatibility; evaluate replacement models or external crypto modules; budget for hardware refresh; confirm FIPS validation of replacement platforms.

blockers.blocker: Microsoft has not released a PQC plugin for Exchange.
blockers.reason: Email signing and encryption using ML-DSA and ML-KEM cannot be deployed in Exchange until Microsoft provides and validates PQC support; no confirmed delivery date exists.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain Microsoft roadmap commitment with dates; monitor release; require FIPS validation evidence; plan email migration as a later phase dependent on vendor delivery.

blockers.blocker: Technical team has zero PQC experience.
blockers.reason: Lack of PQC knowledge risks design errors, insecure hybrid configurations, and failed deployments; training and hiring are prerequisites for safe implementation.
blockers.resolution_required: Fund training on NIST FIPS 203/204/205, hybrid key exchange, and crypto-agility; hire or contract PQC specialists; establish lab for hands-on learning.

blockers.blocker: Change freeze from November 15 to January 15 restricts production changes.
blockers.reason: Production cutovers cannot occur during the freeze, compressing available deployment windows and requiring careful scheduling of phased rollouts.
blockers.resolution_required: Plan all production changes outside freeze windows; obtain exception approval only if critical; use freeze periods for planning, testing, and documentation.

blockers.blocker: Mandate requires only NIST-standardized algorithms (FIPS 203, 204, 205) by 2030.
blockers.reason: Any interim or hybrid solution must ultimately converge on FIPS-validated ML-KEM and ML-DSA; non-standard or unvalidated algorithms cannot be used in production.
blockers.resolution_required: Ensure all procured solutions have FIPS validation or a clear validation path; track NIST validation status; design hybrid modes that use only standardized algorithms.

blockers.blocker: Budget of $2,000,000 may be insufficient for full hardware refresh and software licensing.
blockers.reason: Replacing Cisco routers and licensing PQC-capable software across the enterprise could exceed available funds, especially with training and testing costs.
blockers.resolution_required: Conduct detailed cost analysis; prioritize highest-risk systems; seek supplemental funding or phased procurement; consider overlay solutions to reduce hardware costs.

vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Official Cisco PQC roadmap with dates, hardware compatibility matrix, FIPS 140-3 validation certificates for PQC-capable firmware, and contractual commitment.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Not available. No PQC plugin for Exchange has been released; delivery date unconfirmed.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Official Microsoft announcement of PQC plugin release, FIPS validation evidence, Exchange compatibility documentation, and support lifecycle commitment.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Unconfirmed. ML-DSA certificate issuance and management support must be verified.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Vendor statement on ML-DSA support, FIPS validation, and integration documentation for document signing workflows.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Unconfirmed. ML-KEM support in VPN concentrators and clients must be validated.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: FIPS validation certificates, interoperability test results, and confirmed release dates for ML-KEM hybrid mode.

algorithm_roles.ML-KEM: Post-quantum key establishment (FIPS 203) for VPN key exchange and email encryption key transport; used in hybrid mode with classical algorithms during transition.
algorithm_roles.ML-DSA: Post-quantum digital signatures (FIPS 204) for document signing, email signing, and authentication; used for integrity and non-repudiation.
